title: DNA Clean-up and Size Selection
author: Ashley Jones
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bwkdpcs6
materials: Aliquot 10-30 μg of DNA into a 1.5 mL eppendorf tube. Increase volume to 200 μL with 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8. DNA quantification must be based on Qubit Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific), or similar device. A high quantity of RNA may be present. Volume can exceed 200 μL, maximum of 600 μL due to tube capacity at later steps (ethanol precipitation).

DNA can be size selected by using polymer and salt solutions to preferentially precipitate high-molecular weight DNA, effectively removing shorter fragments. Key solutions are presented here and some commercially available options are also listed. Choose a size selection solution below that suits your experiment, all work on similar principles. These are 2x solutions that will be mixed with an equal volume of DNA at later steps, therefore the final concentrations will be half of what is listed (1x). A B C 1 Solution (2x) Size selection Recovery 2 4% PVP 360,000, 1.2 M KCl, 20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8 > 10 kb 50-75% 3 3% PVP 360,000, 1.2 M NaCl, 20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8 > 25 kb 30-60% 4 9% PEG 8,000, 1 M NaCl, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8 >10 kb Needs more testing 5 Short-Read Eliminator XS (Circulomics) > 10 kb 50-75% 6 Short-Read Eliminator (Circulomics) > 25 kb 30-60% 7 Short-Read Eliminator XL (Circulomics) > 40 kb Size selection and recovery estimates are based on high-molecular weight DNA from non-model species; results may vary considerably. Expect higher loss if DNA is significantly sheared. If the DNA sample is very contaminated, size selection may perform poorly or the DNA may not precipitate.

Aliquot 3-9 μg of DNA into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf DNA LoBind tube. Adjust the volume to exactly 60 μL using 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8 (alternatively buffer EB if using a Circulomics product). DNA mass must be measured by Qubit Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) or equivalent. DNA must not contain high levels of salts, polyphenols, polysaccharides or other contaminants. If you want to add more DNA, increase the volume slightly (also more size selection solution later). For example, 12 μg of DNA in 100 μL (adding 100 μL of size selection solution later).

steps.title: Add RNase A and Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL RNase A (stock 20 mg/mL, final 100 µg/mL) and 1 µL Proteinase K (stock 20 mg/mL, final 100 µg/mL) to each sample.

steps.title: Incubate for enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate the samples at 55 °C (acceptable range 50‑60 °C) for 20 min while shaking at 400‑500 rpm if possible.

steps.title: Adjust volume with Tris‑HCl
steps.instruction: Increase the total volume to 600 µL by adding 400 µL of 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8.

steps.title: First chloroform‑isoamyl extraction
steps.instruction: Add 600 µL (equal volume) of chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1, v/v) and invert the tube 10‑15 times to mix briefly.

steps.title: Phase separation by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16,000 rcf for 1 min at 20 °C (or room temperature) to separate phases.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Second chloroform‑isoamyl extraction
steps.instruction: Repeat the chloroform:isoamyl alcohol clean‑up by adding an equal volume (600 µL) and mixing as before, then centrifuge as above and retain the aqueous phase.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with ethanol and acetate
steps.instruction: To the aqueous phase add 1.5 × volume of 100 % ethanol (~900 µL) and 0.1 × volume of 3 M sodium acetate, pH 5.2 (~60 µL); invert to mix thoroughly. Ensure the total volume does not exceed 600 µL after the chloroform clean‑up.

steps.title: Pellet DNA by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16,000 rcf for 1 min at 20 °C (or room temperature). If no pellet is visible, pulse‑spin for 10 s at maximum speed or extend the spin time. Optionally increase ethanol concentration to 2 × volume.

steps.title: First 70 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add ~700 µL freshly prepared 70 % ethanol (enough to cover the pellet).

steps.title: Centrifuge after first ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16,000 rcf for 1 min at 20 °C (or room temperature).

steps.title: Second 70 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the addition of ~700 µL 70 % ethanol and centrifuge as above.

steps.title: Air‑dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Place the tube upside‑down on tissue paper and air‑dry for 5‑15 min at room temperature until all ethanol has evaporated. Avoid water contacting the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA in Tris‑HCl
steps.instruction: Dissolve the DNA pellet in 60 µL of 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8.

steps.title: Quantify DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer and a Qubit fluorometer (dsDNA broad‑range assay).

steps.title: Optional needle shearing
steps.instruction: If desired, perform needle shearing: choose a needle (e.g., 29 G for 10‑20 kb N50, 5 passes; 26 G for 20‑35 kb N50, 5 passes). Connect the needle to a syringe and aspirate‑dispense 5 times. Note that shearing is optional and usually skipped.

steps.title: Aliquot DNA for size selection
steps.instruction: Aliquot 3‑9 µg DNA into a 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tube and adjust the volume to exactly 60 µL with 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8.

steps.title: Perform needle passes (if shearing)
steps.instruction: Connect the chosen needle to a syringe and perform 5 passes (aspirate and dispense 5 times).

steps.title: Add size‑selection solution
steps.instruction: Add 60 µL (equal volume) of the selected size‑selection solution and mix gently by tapping or pipetting up‑and‑down.

steps.title: Centrifuge for size selection
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10,000 rcf for 30 min at 20 °C (or room temperature). Mark the tube orientation to locate the DNA pellet; low temperatures (e.g., 4 °C) reduce recovery.

steps.title: Remove supernatant carefully
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, remove the supernatant as soon as possible without disturbing the fragile pellet. Mark the expected pellet spot and optionally keep the supernatant in a separate tube.

steps.title: First 70 % ethanol wash (post‑selection)
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL freshly prepared 70 % ethanol to cover the pellet; do not tap or mix after addition.

steps.title: Centrifuge after first post‑selection wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10,000 rcf for 2 min at 20 °C (or room temperature).

steps.title: Second 70 % ethanol wash (post‑selection)
steps.instruction: Repeat the addition of 200 µL 70 % ethanol and centrifugation as above.

steps.title: Air‑dry final DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Place the tube upside‑down on tissue paper and air‑dry for 5‑15 min at room temperature until all ethanol has evaporated. Avoid water contacting the pellet.

steps.title: Hydrate DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Let the pellet hydrate at room temperature for ~10 min; if it does not dissolve, incubate at 50 °C for 10 min (avoid longer incubations to limit shearing).

steps.title: Resuspend hydrated DNA
steps.instruction: Gently tap the tube to ensure the DNA is fully resuspended and mixed.

steps.title: Second DNA quantification
steps.instruction: Quantify the DNA again using a Nanodrop and a Qubit fluorometer (dsDNA broad‑range assay).

steps.title: Store DNA at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Store the DNA at 4 °C (in the refrigerator) to avoid freeze‑thaw cycles; extended storage at this temperature does not affect integrity.

steps.title: Incubate sample on ice
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample on ice for 1 min.

steps.title: Decant supernatant without disturbing pellet
steps.instruction: Carefully decant the supernatant as soon as possible without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Soak pellet to dissolve salts
steps.instruction: Let the pellet soak for 1 min at room temperature to dissolve excess salts.

steps.title: Final resuspension in Tris‑HCl
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8 (or EB buffer if using a Circulomics product) and mix by gently tapping the tube.
